question.problem:
Consider the absolute value equation 

$$
2-|x+2|=-7.
$$

This equation can be expressed in the following equivalent form:

$|x+2|=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We can rearrange the equation to isolate the absolute value on the left side:

First, we subtract $2$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-|x+2|=-7 \\ 2-|x+2|-2=-7-2 \\ -|x+2|=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-|x+2| & =-9 \\ (-1)\cdot (-|x+2|) & =(-1)\cdot (-9) \\ (\cancel{-}1)\cdot (\cancel{-}|x+2|) & =9 \\ |x+2| & =9\end{aligned}
$$
